key_insight: Short-wave instabilities in a helical vortex saturate weakly at small linear growth rates but substantially deform the vortex at larger growth rates as higher-order nonlinear effects become important.
engineering_relevance: These dynamics could inform wind-turbine tip-vortex control strategies aimed at accelerating wake recovery and improving turbine performance.
method: Direct numerical simulations of a helical vortex with axial flow disturbed by elliptic or curvature instability modes.
Systematic variation of normalized vortex core radius and reduced pitch.
Comparison of nonlinear evolution with weakly nonlinear analysis.
evidence_signal: Across the simulated parameter range, both instabilities preserve vortex and mode structures at relatively small growth rates but reach higher disturbance energies and substantial deformation at larger growth rates.
watch_item: The study uses an idealized helical vortex; turbine-scale control benefits are not demonstrated in the abstract.
paper_title: Nonlinear dynamics of short-wave instabilities in a helical vortex within and beyond the weakly nonlinear regime
